content.text:
Bangkok has a strong group of schools for both IGCSE and the IB Diploma. They fall into three groups: schools that offer IGCSE and then the IB, IB-only schools, and British schools that follow IGCSE with A Levels instead of the IB. Unless noted, the figures below are the schools' own published results.

## Schools offering both IGCSE and the IB Diploma

**Bangkok Patana School** is the strongest choice if you want IGCSE followed by the IB at the same school. For the Class of 2026, the school reported
21% scoring 40 points or above, a 98.5% pass rate, an average total score of 36 points, and one student achieving the highest score of 45
66 per cent of (I)GCSE results were grades 7-9
. Patana stands out because it is
non-selective and not-for-profit
, so these results aren't the product of entrance tests. It is
Thailand's first and largest British international school

.

**St Andrews International School Sukhumvit 107** is a smaller school with a rising record. Its 2026 IB students
achieved an average score of 36.3 points, out of a maximum of 45, the highest ever IBDP average recorded by the school
, with
a 100% pass rate across both the IBDP and the IB Career-related Programme
. The school also offers
the English National Curriculum and the International Baccalaureate Programme

.

**Dulwich College Bangkok** also offers IB. Its website shows
37.3 average points out of 45

for 2026, but that figure covers the whole Dulwich College International group, not the Bangkok campus alone. Ask the school for its Bangkok-only results.

## IB-only schools (no IGCSE)

- **NIST International School** usually has the highest IB results in the city. For the Class of 2026,

three students achieved the highest possible score of 45 points, while 28% achieved 40 points or above. Among students awarded the IB Diploma, the average score was 37 out of 45, with a 98% pass rate.
It is
Thailand's first full not-for-profit IB World School, offering the complete IB continuum (PYP, MYP, DP)

.
- **International School Bangkok (ISB)** is an American-curriculum school that also offers the IB. In 2026,
94 students earned the full IB Diploma, with a strong average score of 35 points, well above the global average of 30.8

.
- **KIS International School:** In 2024, KIS reported
an average IB Diploma score of 35 for successful candidates, 83% of students scoring above 30 points, and a high score of 44 points

.

## Top IGCSE schools that continue to A Levels, not the IB

- **Harrow International School Bangkok** reported
70% A*-A, 90% A*-B at A level and 71% A*-A, 92% A*-B at IGCSE in 2025

.
- **Shrewsbury International School (Riverside):** In 2025,
at IGCSE, 74% of grades were awarded at A*/A
. At A Level, results were
39 per cent A*, 64 per cent A*/A and 83 per cent A*-B

.

## How to compare the numbers
- **Benchmark:**
For the May 2026 examination session, the average IB Diploma score was 30.8 points out of a possible 45.

- **Selective vs. non-selective:** A selective school's high average partly reflects who gets admitted. Patana's 36 with an open intake is arguably more impressive than a similar score at a selective school.
- **Cohort size:** One ranking puts SISB at the top with
37.4 points (2022, approx. 14 students)

. Averages from very small groups like that aren't comparable with NIST or Patana, which each have well over 100 IB students.
- **Ask schools for:** the share of students who take the full Diploma rather than individual IB courses, whether the average counts all candidates or only those who passed, and university destinations.

**In short:** For IGCSE followed by the IB, Bangkok Patana is the clear front-runner, with St Andrews 107 a strong smaller option. If you only care about the IB, NIST has the highest results among the large schools. If your child will stay on the British track through A Levels, Harrow and Shrewsbury are the leaders.
